events.what: Gordon claims an explicit construction of universal point sets for planar graphs of size n^{1+o(1)} (n·exp(O(sqrt(log n)))) via 213-avoiding permutation superpatterns
events.credibility_reason: Single-version preprint 12 days old with heavy AI involvement in the construction and proof; the Lean formalisation explicitly covers only an earlier construction, not the layered proof; the only commentary found (llmrumors.com) treats it as unverified. No identified error.
events.ai_basis: Starting from the author's interval-based approach, the model helped develop the construction, formulate and revise the proof, check finite examples, and draft the exposition.

judgement.doubts: Scope call: JUDGE.md F3 cites universal point sets as an example where n^{1+o(1)} does not close a linear-versus-quadratic gap. But this bullet's wording asks only for universal point sets of subquadratic size, and n^{1+o(1)} is subquadratic, so against the bullet's own words the claim is whole. If the question is instead read as the gap between linear and quadratic (as Wikipedia's article phrases it), the scope becomes bound and the status becomes progress. AI role is assisted: the model helped develop the construction and proof, which is mathematics in the result, not just checking. The Lean build does not cover the claimed theorem (F10). I did not read the Pith Review page, and it is not verification anyway (F11).

corrections.why: F3: kept as claimed because the bullet asks only for 'subquadratic size', and the claimed n^{1+o(1)} construction answers that in full. Doubt: if the problem is read as closing the linear–quadratic gap (the framing in the record's summary), this is a bound and the status would be progress.
